title: Kingston, Ontario
summary: A small Camarilla city that guards the St. Lawrence route and the Sabbat border.

claims.text: Only four Camarilla Kindred hold Kingston, a city too small by rights to feed even one; its universities and prisons make it worth the trouble, and it sits where Camarilla and Sabbat lands meet at the head of the St. Lawrence.

Prince Iain MacLaren, a ninth-generation Ventrue banker Embraced in London in 1874, took the city after leaving Britain in 1979; a paid arrangement with Lucian of Gary to move Kindred down the river into the States funds the post.
The Brujah Angelique Cormier, a Quebec native barred from going home, spends nights lobbying the Camarilla to take Quebec from the Sabbat, and treats a destroyed sire as a martyr to that cause.
A Camarilla Samedi named Driscoll works nights as a janitor at the penitentiary and controls who feeds on its inmates; the old Gangrel Merill Olsen keeps out of local politics altogether.
The local Kindred are said to stage well-timed crashes on Highway 401 to strand rivals who travel by night.

title: Carfax Abbey
summary: A London goth club in a gutted church where anarchs gather.

claims.text: Carfax Abbey is a new goth dance club built inside an old London church: a maze of alcoves, three bars, a dance floor and a stage, open to any vampire and the main meeting ground for the city's growing anarch crowd.

Its ancilla owner, Holden, argued to Lady Anne that a club full of mortals dressed as vampires is the safest place for real ones to hide; the prince lets it stand, partly because it keeps the anarchs in one place that would burn easily.
Holden's ghouls, each trained a little in Celerity, throw out rowdy mortals, while a Brujah security chief handles trouble from the Kindred.
The house band Persephone Seed has two Kindred members, and vampires come to watch them flout the Masquerade on stage.
